metadata.title: 1971 Case 04
metadata.original_presentation: A 71-year-old woman was admitted to the hospital because of dyspnea.

required.content: What is the patient's past medical history?
required.response: The patient underwent abdominoperineal resection for rectal carcinoma three years earlier, with a left-sided colostomy, appendectomy, and hysterectomy. She had a history of malignant lymphoma with previous radiation therapy.

teaching_points.content: Past medical history, especially cancer and surgical history, is crucial in understanding current presentations and potential complications.

required.content: What symptoms did the patient experience before admission?
required.response: The patient experienced dyspnea, peripheral edema, redness and swelling of both breasts, anorexia, weakness, cough, and progressive dyspnea.

teaching_points.content: Symptoms such as dyspnea and edema can indicate underlying systemic issues, including cardiac or pulmonary complications.

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Congestive Heart Failure
refuting_evidence: redness and swelling of both breasts is atypical

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Pulmonary Embolism
refuting_evidence: peripheral edema and breast symptoms are atypical

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Breast Cancer with Metastasis
supporting_evidence: redness and swelling of both breasts
refuting_evidence: dyspnea and peripheral edema are atypical for primary breast cancer

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Lymphedema secondary to Radiation Therapy
supporting_evidence: history of malignant lymphoma with radiation therapy
refuting_evidence: dyspnea and breast symptoms are atypical

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD)
refuting_evidence: no history of smoking provided
peripheral edema and breast symptoms are atypical

required.content: What were the findings on physical examination?
required.response: The patient was thin, tachypneic, and appeared severely ill. Cyanosis of lips and nails was noted. A mass was present on the right side of the pharynx. Crackling inspiratory rales were heard at both lung bases. A Grade 2 musical systolic murmur was present at the cardiac apex.

teaching_points.content: Physical examination can reveal critical signs such as cyanosis and rales, indicating respiratory distress and potential cardiac involvement.

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Congestive Heart Failure
refuting_evidence: mass on the right side of the pharynx
history of cancer

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Pulmonary Embolism
refuting_evidence: peripheral edema
crackling rales

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Lymphoma Recurrence
supporting_evidence: mass on the right side of the pharynx
refuting_evidence: crackling rales
systolic murmur

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Metastatic Cancer
supporting_evidence: mass on the right side of the pharynx
refuting_evidence: systolic murmur
crackling rales
additional_information_needed: CT scan of the chest and abdomen

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Pneumonia
refuting_evidence: mass on the right side of the pharynx
systolic murmur

required.content: What were the key test results and diagnostic procedures?
required.response: X-ray films showed bilateral pleural effusions and mediastinal lymphadenopathy. Biopsy of a cervical lymph node showed malignant lymphoma. Blood tests showed anemia and leukocytosis. Arterial blood gases indicated hypoxemia and respiratory alkalosis.

teaching_points.content: Imaging and biopsy are essential for diagnosing and staging malignancies. Blood gas analysis helps assess respiratory function.

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Recurrent Malignant Lymphoma
key_features: cervical lymph node biopsy showing malignant lymphoma
supporting_evidence: biopsy of a cervical lymph node showed malignant lymphoma
additional_information_needed: PET scan to assess the extent of lymphoma
further histological analysis to determine lymphoma subtype

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Pleural Effusion secondary to Malignancy
supporting_evidence: X-ray films showed bilateral pleural effusions
history of rectal carcinoma and lymphoma
additional_information_needed: cytology of pleural fluid to check for malignant cells

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Congestive Heart Failure
supporting_evidence: Grade 2 musical systolic murmur at the cardiac apex
refuting_evidence: no clear evidence of heart enlargement or pulmonary venous congestion on X-ray

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Pulmonary Embolism
refuting_evidence: no mention of acute onset or risk factors such as recent surgery or immobilization

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Infectious Pneumonia
supporting_evidence: crackling inspiratory rales at both lung bases
refuting_evidence: no fever or purulent sputum reported
mediastinal lymphadenopathy more suggestive of malignancy

required.content: What treatments were administered during the hospital stay?
required.response: The patient received oxygen therapy, prednisone, heparin, and furosemide. Ventilatory assistance was provided during respiratory arrest.

teaching_points.content: Management of respiratory distress includes oxygen therapy and addressing underlying causes. Steroids and anticoagulation may be used in specific contexts.

final_diagnosis.name: Malignant lymphoma with respiratory complications
supporting_evidence: Imaging showing pleural effusions and lymphadenopathy
